targetAudience.primary: Storage, artifact-service, runtime and reliability engineers
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands versioned artifacts, filesystem rename and concurrent writers.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A system can expose a complete version atomically and still lack crash durability, while a single Published flag hides ownership, completeness, visibility and persistence as different lifecycle facts.

whyNow: A same-day merged Google ADK implementation reserves hidden pending versions, stages payload and metadata, rechecks the destination and exposes the completed tree through rename while explicitly excluding fsync-backed power-loss durability.

externalHook.description: The instant readers can see a complete version is not the same instant storage has proven it will survive a crash.

coreProposition: Artifact publication should model reservation, staged completeness, reader visibility and durable persistence as separate lifecycle facts: pending isolation plus atomic rename can establish process-level visibility under stated filesystem assumptions, but rename success is not crash-durability evidence and abandoned-state recovery needs independent ownership proof.

originalValue.description: Turns an implementation-specific pending-directory protocol into a four-state engineering model that prevents atomic visibility, durability and recovery authority from collapsing into one success flag.

readerTakeaway: Hide incomplete state structurally, arbitrate writer ownership in the relevant fault domain, publish through an explicit visibility boundary, and require separate evidence for durability and stale-owner cleanup.

supported: Hidden pending directories are ignored by ordinary integer-version discovery.
Payload and metadata are staged before one os.replace makes the complete tree visible.
Directory creation arbitrates reservations and a destination recheck prevents stale-list overwrite.
The maintainers explicitly exclude full power-loss durability without fsync.
Abandoned reservations may leave permanent version gaps when stale ownership cannot be proven.
unsupported: Automatic safe reclamation of abandoned reservations
Equivalent rename semantics on every filesystem
uncertain: Which filesystem capabilities should be verified before relying on rename
How to garbage-collect pending state without misclassifying a slow live writer

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general storage-publication and recovery pattern without first-party project dependence.

decisionReason: The source provides explicit code, tests and limitation statements, while the Research Object adds a reusable lifecycle distinction with clear operational consequences.
